title: Retrieval-augmented Generation to Improve Math Question-Answering: Trade-offs Between Groundedness and Human Preference
venue: NeurIPS’23 Workshop on Generative AI for Education (GAIED)
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can improve the quality of AI-generated responses to middle-school mathematics questions, and whether increased grounding in a textbook necessarily makes responses better for users. The authors are motivated by concerns that LLMs used for math tutoring can hallucinate, give incorrect answers, or produce responses that are poorly aligned with a school’s curriculum.

To study this, they built a RAG-based math question-answering system using sections from the OpenStax Prealgebra textbook as the retrieval corpus and GPT-3.5 as the response model. They varied prompt guidance across several conditions: no retrieval guidance, low guidance, high guidance, and a retrieval-only condition. They first evaluated groundedness on 51 real student questions from the Math Nation discussion board, then surveyed 9 educators and education-technology designers who ranked the responses and judged whether they were grounded in the textbook. They also annotated the relevance of retrieved documents.

The paper finds that retrieval and prompt guidance can increase groundedness, but that the most grounded responses are not always the most preferred. In particular, low-guidance RAG responses were preferred over both no-guidance and high-guidance responses, while high-guidance responses were perceived as more grounded. The authors conclude that math QA systems need to balance faithfulness to source materials with student preference and conversational usefulness, and they highlight the need for future work involving real middle-school students and actual learning outcomes.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a small, non-randomized evaluation study with human ratings rather than a causal learning experiment. It is methodologically careful for a prototype paper, but it is still primarily a qualitative/comparative system evaluation with limited external validity.
impact_tier_rationale: The system shows promising preference and groundedness results for a priority population context, but there is no direct evidence of learning gains or practical impact. The study suggests design value for math tutoring systems, yet the impact on student outcomes remains unclear.

interventions.use_case: retrieval-augmented conversational math tutoring for middle-school algebra and geometry question answering, using GPT-3.5 with prompts that vary the degree of textbook grounding

finding.finding_summary: The paper does not measure student learning directly; instead it evaluates math QA response quality for middle-school algebra and geometry questions. Humans preferred the low-guidance RAG responses over no-guidance and high-guidance responses, while high guidance produced the highest groundedness (mean groundedness 0.90 vs 0.59 low and 0.52 none).
finding.measure: Human preference rankings and groundedness judgments on generated answers to 51 middle-school math questions
finding.study_size: n=51 queries; n=9 annotators; n=153 groundedness ratings
